packages.statement: Client Connector for Linux can be installed manually with the application package, the Debian package or the Red Hat Package Manager (RPM) package, or through a device management method that supports Linux devices. Installation needs administrator permission, and the Debian package is obtained from Zscaler Support.

quotes: You can use the application package, the Debian package, or the Red Hat Package Manager (RPM) to manually install Zscaler Client Connector on a device.
You can also use these packages if you're deploying the app to users through a device management method that supports Linux devices.
You must have administrator permission to do the installation. Contact Zscaler Support to obtain the Debian package.

dns-and-networkmanager.statement: Client Connector for Linux relies on the systemd-resolved service to manage DNS, so /etc/resolv.conf, a symbolic link to /run/systemd/resolve/stub-resolv.conf, should not be modified when deploying it; it also requires NetworkManager and its CLI, nmcli.

quotes: Zscaler Client Connector relies on the Linux systemd-resolved service to manage DNS configurations.
Because /etc/resolv.conf is a symbolic link to /run/systemd/resolve/stub-resolv.conf, you should not modify the /etc/resolv.conf file when deploying Zscaler Client Connector for Linux.
Zscaler Client Connector requires NetworkManager and its CLI, nmcli

dependencies.statement: As long as the device is connected to the network, the installer installs the necessary package dependencies automatically; if they do not install, they can be installed manually by entering all of them on one command line without line breaks. CentOS 9 Stream and RHEL 9 have an additional package, systemd-resolved, from the EPEL repository, which must be installed separately; for CentOS the EPEL repository must be enabled for Qt packages, and qt5-qtwebengine is also part of EPEL.

quotes: As long as your device is connected to the network, the application installer automatically installs the necessary package dependencies for you.
If dependencies don't automatically install, you can install them manually by entering all dependencies in a command line on one line without line breaks
CentOS 9 Stream has an additional package, systemd-resolved, that is part of the Extra Packages for Enterprise Linux (EPEL) repository which must be installed separately for CentOS.
The CentOS OS is required to enable the EPEL repository for Qt packages.
RHEL 9 has an additional package, systemd-resolved, that is part of the Extra Packages for Enterprise Linux (EPEL) repository which must be installed separately for RHEL 9.
The qt5-qtwebengine is also part of the EPEL repository.

run-file.statement: The Linux run file is downloaded from the Client Connector App Store on the Client Connector Portal, made executable with chmod, and installed with sudo ./Zscaler-linux-<version number>-installer.run, leaving the token form empty. It takes the install options --cloudName, --deviceToken, --hideAppUIOnLaunch, --policyToken, --strictEnforcement, --userDomain and --enableFips.

quotes: Download the Zscaler run file from the Zscaler Client Connector App Store on the Zscaler Client Connector Portal.
sudo chmod a+x Zscaler-linux-<version number>-installer.run
sudo ./Zscaler-linux-<version number>-installer.run
Leave the token form empty.
Replace <install options> with one or more of the following options:

evidence.after: Replace <install options> with one or more of the following options:
quotes: --cloudName
--deviceToken
--hideAppUIOnLaunch
--policyToken
--strictEnforcement
--userDomain
--enableFips

option-notes.statement: On Linux, --deviceToken applies only to Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) and is not supported by Zscaler Private Access (ZPA); --hideAppUIOnLaunch, --strictEnforcement and --enableFips default to 0 (disabled).

quotes: The --deviceToken install option only applies to Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA). It is not supported by Zscaler Private Access (ZPA).
To enable this option using the CLI, enter --hideAppUIOnLaunch 1. By default, the value is 0 (i.e., disabled).
To enable this option using the CLI, enter --strictEnforcement 1. By default, the value is 0 (i.e., disabled).
This install option allows you to enable the Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) mode for Zscaler Client Connector. By default, the value is 0 (i.e., disabled).

debian.statement: The Debian package is a silent installer that does not allow any arguments to pass next to it; installation parameters are configured in interactive or silent mode. The packages are named zscaler-client_<version number>_amd64.deb and zscaler-client-debug_<version number>_amd64.deb; Zscaler recommends installing systemd-coredump first, and a run-file installation must be uninstalled before the Debian package is installed.

quotes: The Debian package is a silent installer and does not allow any arguments to pass next to it.
Configure installation parameters using either interactive or silent mode.
zscaler-client_<version number>_amd64.deb
zscaler-client-debug_<version number>_amd64.deb
Zscaler recommends installing systemd-coredump before installing the Zscaler Client Connector Debian package.
first uninstall the Zscaler run file before installing the Debian package

zscaler-config.statement: The zscaler-config script edits the parameters in /opt/zscaler/.config.ini; only administrators can use it to edit the configuration after the Debian package is installed, and it requires root permission. It can be run without parameters (sudo zscaler-config), or with the flags -c Cloud Name, -d User Domain, -f Enable Fips, -h Help, -l hideAppUIOnLaunch, -p User password, -r externalRedirect, -s strictEnforcement, -t policyToken, -T deviceToken, -u username and -w waitForInput.

quotes: The configuration script zscaler-config resolves this issue. This script edits the parameters in this file:
/opt/zscaler/.config.ini.
Only administrators can use zscaler-config to edit the parameter configuration after the Debian package is installed on the system and requires root permission.
Run zscaler-config without parameters (e.g., sudo zscaler-config).

zscaler-config - [ -c Cloud Name ] [-d User Domain ] [ -f Enable Fips ] [ -h Help] [ -l hideAppUIOnLaunch ] [ -p User password ] [ -r externalRedirect ] [ -s strictEnforcement ] [ -t policyToken ] [ -T deviceToken ] [ -u username ] [ -w waitForInput ]

rpm.statement: Client Connector for Linux supports the RPM distributions RHEL, Fedora, CentOS and openSUSE. Zscaler_package_installation.sh identifies the distribution and installs the corresponding dependencies, and Zscaler-client-<release version>-1.x86_64.rpm installs the Client Connector binaries. The CLI steps for Client Connector 3.7.1 and later for openSUSE use sudo zypper install zscaler-client-3.7.1.51-1.x86_64.rpm.

quotes: Zscaler Client Connector for Linux supports the following RPM distributions: RHEL, Fedora, CentOS, and openSUSE.

Zscaler_package_installation.sh: Zscaler Client Connector installation requires different dependencies based on the respective distribution. This script identifies the distribution and installs the corresponding dependencies.
Zscaler-client-<release version>-1.x86_64.rpm: This file installs Zscaler Client Connector binaries in each system.
To download and install the CLI version of the RPM Package for Zscaler Client Connector version 3.7.1 and later for Linux, follow these steps:
For openSUSE, enter sudo zypper install zscaler-client-3.7.1.51-1.x86_64.rpm.

logs.statement: On Linux, tray logs are in <user home>/.Zscaler/Logs, Zscaler system logs in /var/log/zscaler/.Zscaler/Logs, and installer errors in /var/log/zscaler/zscaler-installation.log.

quotes: Tray logs: <user home>/.Zscaler/Logs
Zscaler system logs: /var/log/zscaler/.Zscaler/Logs
Installer errors: /var/log/zscaler/zscaler-installation.log

dependency-lists.title: Which dependency list belongs to which Linux distribution
dependency-lists.detail: The capture flattens the Linux page's tabs, so the per-distribution package dependency lists cannot be read from it; claim distributions names the distributions only.

config-parameters.title: What externalRedirect, waitForInput, MAPubKey and the -S switch do, and where zscaler-config applies
config-parameters.detail: The page lists externalRedirect and waitForInput as zscaler-config flags and its detailed usage also lists -S to disable the sudo keyword inside the scripts, and the RPM parameter list names MAPubKey; the page does not describe what these do, and does not say whether zscaler-config applies to a run-file installation.
